relations.subject: eventing:on-delete-handler
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - minted in Capella twin; requoted fresh from this Server page
relations.evidence: Create a JavaScript Function that contains an **OnDelete** handler, which runs whenever a document is deleted or expired (or mutated). The Eventing Function merely logs whether the document was deleted or was expired from a collection. This function accesses the 'expired' field of the second optional argument to the handler.

relations.subject: eventing:expired-flag
relations.evidence:
When its expiration time is reached, an item is deleted as soon as one of the following occurs:

  * An attempt is made to access the item.
  * The expiry pager is run (default every 60 minutes).
  * Compaction is run.

relations.subject: eventing:function

notable_absence.finding: This page cites the same historical macOS defect the Capella twin flagged as a durable dependency on an external, closeable Jira ticket: 'On macOS (or OS-X) if you get a 'dyld: Library not loaded' when running _cbc_ a solution is documented in [MB-37768](https://issues.couchbase.com/browse/MB-37768).' On the Server tree this is not a content-bleed risk the way it was on the Capella twin - cbc and its macOS/Linux/Windows install paths are entirely native, on-topic content for a self-managed product - but the same fragile external-ticket dependency risk still applies verbatim to this page.

cross_product_finding: The Capella twin's own extraction flagged the cbc binary paths and Python/Java SDK prerequisite steps on this page as 'self-managed content bleed' into a Capella doc, citing the same Linux path (/opt/couchbase/bin/cbc) and Windows path (C:\Program Files\Couchbase\Server\bin\cbc) verbatim. Reading the Server original confirms the hypothesis directly: this Server page contains the identical four-tab prerequisite (SQL++ UPSERT, cbc binary, Python SDK script, Java SDK program) with the same Linux/macOS/Windows cbc paths, word for word - meaning the Capella page's prerequisite section was very likely copied from this Server page rather than authored fresh for a managed-cluster audience where users have no shell access to a Couchbase Server bin directory at all.
